evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.10.4: nostra ad diem dictam fient (Lewis & Short s.v. ad)
Caes. BG 2.5: omnia ad diem facta sunt (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 86: by January, ad mēnsem Jānuārium; by the sixth hour, ad sextam hōram
terms.comment: What is due or done by a set day: ad diem, on the day, punctually. “By now” is jam (see already).

evidence: Liv. 42.45.1: lēgātiō sub idem tempus in Asiam et circum īnsulās missa (Lewis & Short s.v. sub)
Traupman 88: around the time of, sub tempus (+ gen.); at about the same time, sub idem tempus
terms.comment: Close to a time, on either side of it: sub noctem, towards nightfall (see just before nightfall).

phrases.latin: quam ad diem legiōnī frūmentum dēbērī sciēbat
phrases.english: the day on which, as he knew, corn was due to the legion
